# l5r-rules — guide for AI assistants

> l5r-rules (https://l5r-rules.web.app) is a website for playing Legend of the Five Rings,
> fourth edition: a searchable rulebook, character sheets, and shared campaigns. This guide
> tells an AI assistant how to use it on behalf of a Game Master (GM) who runs a campaign.

## How you use it

- There is no API. Use the website in a browser, the way a person would: click buttons, fill
  fields, read the page. Everything below names the visible button text.
- Sign-in is with Google ("Sign in with Google"). The person signs in; never type passwords.
- The site saves as you go. There is no global Save; editors have their own Save buttons.
- Deleting or removing asks for confirmation in a browser dialog (OK/Cancel). Do not delete
  anything the GM did not ask you to delete. Browser-automation tools can get stuck on these
  dialogs: tell the GM before you click a Delete/Remove button.
- Changes are live for every player at once. Players see what you write.
- Do not reload pages in a loop: the site runs on a free database quota.
- Rules questions: the books are on the site (Books, All pages). Official errata overrides
  the printed rules.

## Addresses

- `#/start` — start page: Campaigns, Characters, Books, Library.
- `#/campaigns/<title>-<id>` — a campaign. Sections: `/timeline` (the map), `/sessions`,
  `/plots`, `/npcs`, `/pcs`, then optionally `/<item name>-<id>` to open one item.
  Only the id part matters; names in links may be out of date after a rename.
- `#/characters/<name>-<id>` — a character sheet you own. `#/create-character` makes one.
- `#/pc/<owner>/<id>` — someone else's character, public view.
- `#/library` — the media library (pictures for maps, NPCs and sessions).
- `#/books`, `#/all-pages`, `#/books/<book>/<page>` — the rules.

## Who can do what in a campaign

- **GMs.** A campaign can have several. The lead GM made the campaign; extra GMs do
  everything the lead GM does except delete the campaign. Any GM makes a player GM too
  ("Make GM") or takes an extra GM off ("Remove GM"; "Stop being GM" for yourself).
- **Players** add their PCs, write in session journals, write plots, and place their own
  tokens on the map.
- **Nothing is secret inside a campaign.** Every member can read every session, plot, NPC
  and journal entry. Keep GM-only secrets out of the campaign (tell the GM so).
- **Full sheets.** A GM reads every player's full sheet ("Full sheet"); players see each
  other's public view.

## The campaign page

A row of buttons sits on top of the map: Add Session, Add Plot, Add NPC, Add PC, then a
chip for every session (newest first) and every plot. A chip opens that item as a panel.

### Sessions (what happened at each game night)

- **Add Session** → Session title, First entry (what happened), optional pictures
  ("Add image" picks from the Library) → **Save session**.
- Open a session → **Edit** to rename it or change pictures (**Delete session** shows
  while editing). **Add Entry** adds another journal entry (Title, text) → **Save entry**.
- Any member writes in a session's journal. "✓ names" under an item shows who read it.

### Plots (story threads, rumours, quests)

- **Add Plot** → Plot title, First entry → **Save plot**. Any member can add one; the
  GM or the plot's creator edits it (**Edit plot**) and adds entries (**Add Entry**).

### NPCs and places

- **Add NPC** → Name, Role (e.g. "Magistrate of the Lion"), Description, a picture
  (upload, **Create picture**, or **Library**), and the box "Place (a location, not a
  person)" for castles, villages, temples → **Save**.
- Open an NPC → **Edit**. NPC journals are written by GMs only (**Add Entry**).
- The Add NPC popup also has "Edit list" to remove NPCs.

### PCs and players

- **Add PC** opens a popup. A GM sees the **Players** list there: the lead GM first,
  "GM" tags, each player's PCs or "joined · no PC yet", and anyone who asks to join.
- Someone who wants in finds the campaign on the start page and asks to be invited. A GM
  answers: **Approve** (they join when they next open the campaign), **Add now** (they
  join at once, without opening anything), or **Decline**. Requests also show as a notice
  on the campaign page.
- A GM opens a PC with **Full sheet**. **Transfer** gives a PC to another player (they
  must **Accept**). Removing a PC from the campaign keeps the sheet with its player.

### The map (timeline)

- The map shows tokens for PCs, NPCs, places, clans, and numbered journal entries.
- On the left, a tray lists the clans, PCs, people and places, each followed by the
  numbers of its journal entries. Drag a name or a number onto the map; it snaps to the
  hex grid. Drag a token off the map to remove it. Clicking a token opens its item.
- Drop a name onto a clan or onto another name to nest it under it (for example, an NPC
  under their clan); drop it on a group title to take it out.
- Zoom with − 100% + at the top of the map (100%–400%), or Ctrl/⌘ + scroll.
- **GMs only, the map panel at the top right:** "Maps" lists the maps; click one to show
  it, ✎ renames it, ✕ takes it off the list (its tokens are kept), **Add Map** picks a
  picture from the Library. "Cell size" sets the hex grid size of the shown map. Each map
  keeps its own tokens.

### Campaign settings

- A GM edits the campaign title at the top of the page.
- **Delete campaign** (lead GM only) deletes everything for everyone. Never do this
  unless the GM explicitly asks, and confirm first.
- **Leave campaign** — players and extra GMs.

## The library

- `#/library`: pictures added by players, then official Legend of the Five Rings art
  (loaded from legendofthefiverings.com) and the site's own images.
- **Upload** a picture, or paste an image link (https://…) and **Add link**.
- Click a picture to open it large (**Original ↗** opens its source).
- **Remove** hides a picture for you only (**Restore** under "Hidden by you"); on your own
  upload it is **Delete**, which deletes it for everyone.

## Characters

- `#/create-character` or "Add PC" on the start page makes a character; the sheet follows
  the fourth-edition rules (clan, family, school, rings and traits, skills, advantages,
  disadvantages, experience points). **Public view** shows what other players see.
- Journal entries on a sheet have a **Public** box; unticked entries stay private to the
  owner and the GM.

## Good habits for a GM's assistant

- Before a session: add the session with a title and a short first entry; add the NPCs and
  places the players will meet (with Role and Description); put them on the map.
- After a session: add journal entries for what happened, move tokens to where the party
  is, and update plots with new clues.
- Use the GM's language and tone. Keep entries short and readable; the players read them.
- Ask the GM before anything that removes or overwrites content, and before making
  someone a GM or adding a player.
